concept: How are traits passed from parents to their offspring?
title: The Pea Garden
tagline: Cross the peas and watch what never blends

science.hiddenLaw: Mendel's Law of Segregation for autosomal genes: each diploid parent carries two alleles per gene which segregate during meiosis so each gamete receives one allele at random; offspring receive one allele from each parent, restoring diploidy; with complete dominance heterozygotes (Aa) show the dominant phenotype, producing predictable discrete phenotype ratios such as ~3:1 dominant:recessive for Aa × Aa and ~1:1 for Aa × aa, not blending inheritance and not inheritance of acquired somatic changes.
science.plainStatement: Children get one copy of each gene from mom and one from dad at random; some versions (dominant) hide others (recessive) so traits appear in predictable ratios, not as a blend.
misconceptions: Blending inheritance: offspring traits are a smooth average or blend of parental traits producing intermediate phenotypes for single-gene traits.
Lamarckian inheritance of acquired characteristics: traits parents acquire during their lifetime (e.g., muscle, injury, learned behavior) are passed to offspring via genes.

Single-parent or sex-biased inheritance for autosomal traits and 'dominant means most common/strongest': autosomal traits come from only mother or only father, or dominant alleles always become more frequent or physically stronger.

checks.description: Aa × Aa monohybrid cross with complete dominance yields ~75% dominant phenotype, falsifying blending which predicts 100% intermediates
Test cross Aa × aa yields ~50% dominant phenotype, falsifying single-parent-only inheritance
Heterozygous Aa parent transmits allele A to ~50% of offspring, showing random segregation of homologous chromosomes
Discrete inheritance produces no intermediate phenotype class for single-gene complete dominance, falsifying blending
Control: environmentally acquired phenotype in aa parents with unchanged genotype is not transmitted; offspring remain ~0% dominant, falsifying Lamarckian inheritance
